query:
The group settled on dinner first then moving on to a Shoreditch cocktail bar for Joel's birthday. What did Kezia's response to the plan signal about her actual intention for the evening, and what specifically in how she phrased her commitment tells you she wasn't planning to stay for the whole night?

Options:
A. Jess
B. Tom
C. Kezia
D. Rory
context:
[1] (about=Kezia, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:39:00) Probably just dinner. I have a thing.
[2] (about=Aisha, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:36:00) honestly I think dinner then move on. Kezia are you staying for drinks or just dinner?
[3] (about=Aisha, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T22:12:00) I'll book the table for 8. Kezia, are you drinking or should I flag for the waiter?
[4] (about=Kezia, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T22:15:00) Just water is fine.
[5] (about=Kezia, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:30:00) I can attend for the early part.
[6] (about=Kezia, episodic, t2 @2025-01-13T20:36:00) I will come for a bit.
[7] (about=Rory, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:18:00) Shoreditch cocktail bar on a Saturday night 🎉 the contrast with Joel's actual personality is a lot but fine, I'll go. we should do dinner first
[8] (about=Aisha, episodic, t3 @2025-01-20T21:15:00) so Joel's birthday is Feb 1st and Sasha has suggested doing a cocktail bar thing in Shoreditch. not very Joel but anyway. who's in? 🎂
[9] (about=Jess, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:33:00) I'm in! Aisha are we doing dinner first then drinks or just joining for drinks?
[10] (about=Tom, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:27:00) not my thing but if joel wants it I'll show
agent_answer:
Kezia’s responses signaled she intended to come only for the early/dinner part of the evening, not the whole night out at the Shoreditch cocktail bar.

Specifically, she phrased her commitment as:

- “Probably just dinner. I have a thing.”
- “I can attend for the early part.”
- “I will come for a bit.”
- “Just water is fine.”

This shows she was not planning to stay for the drinks/bar portion.

**Answer: C. Kezia**

query:
The Sunday walk is the group's standing commitment. What did Aisha's observation about Marcus reveal about his actual relationship to that norm, and what in the pattern of his responses confirmed this was not a recent or temporary change?

Options:
A. Priya
B. Marcus
C. Kezia
D. Rory
context:
[1] (about=Aisha, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:36:00) Marcus, I noticed you missed again 🙁 third Sunday running. everything ok?
[2] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:39:00) Work. Sorry. Next week I think.
[3] (about=Dan, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:42:00) Marcus I say this with affection: you have been thinking next week for approximately four months.
[4] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T22:00:00) Just a lot of travel at the moment.
[5] (about=Marcus, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:54:00) I'll be out of town that weekend. Enjoy.
[6] (about=Marcus, episodic, t2 @2025-01-13T20:27:00) Can't make tonight. Enjoy.
[7] (about=Jess, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T21:57:00) to be fair Marcus you're always out of town for these things 😄 are you secretly running a second life somewhere
[8] (about=Jess, episodic, t10 @2025-02-10T19:24:00) wait Marcus you just sent a message that was not a response to a direct question?? who are you and what have you done with our Marcus
[9] (about=Kezia, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T20:57:00) I think we should note that Marcus's participation pattern is consistent rather than declining. Arguably this is just how his weekends work, not an avoidance strategy.
[10] (about=Dan, episodic, t4 @2025-01-20T22:03:00) Jess I suspect Marcus simply values his weekends more sensibly than the rest of us. After last week I am in no position to judge.
agent_answer:
Aisha’s observation — that Marcus had missed a third Sunday running — revealed that he does not actually treat the Sunday walk as a real commitment; he regularly skips it with excuses.

The pattern confirming this was long-term, not temporary: Marcus’s replies were repeated excuses (“Can’t make tonight,” “out of town,” “Work. Sorry. Next week I think.”), and others corroborated the history — Dan noted Marcus had been saying “next week” for about four months, and Jess said he was “always out of town for these things.”

**Answer: B. Marcus**

query:
One of the group's unspoken rules was put to a test. What was the norm at stake, who initiated the test, and what specifically in how the group responded revealed that the rule wasn't enforced the same way for everyone?

Options:
A. Kezia
B. Zoe
C. Dan
D. Aisha
context:
[1] (about=Zoe, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:06:00) it is technically a work story but it reads as a comedy of errors and I think the no-work rule has a humanitarian exception clause
[2] (about=Zoe, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:00:00) ok unrelated but I have to tell you all what happened in A&E on Thursday, it is objectively incredible and you need to know
[3] (about=Dan, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:12:00) The rule exists to protect us from spreadsheet updates and line management disputes. A comedy from A&E is categorically distinct. Proceed.
[4] (about=Aisha, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:27:00) to be honest this is the most Zoe has told us about work in all the time she's been in this group, progress 😂
[5] (about=Zoe, episodic, t14 @2025-02-24T21:15:00) ok. man came in with a normal complaint. turns out he had been self-medicating with something he found on a podcast called Health Optimised. I will let you do the maths.
[6] (about=Kezia, episodic, t2 @2025-01-13T21:09:00) I left at 10. I had a reasonable evening. I note that the quiz rounds were poorly structured and the tiebreak question was factually ambiguous.
[7] (about=Dan, episodic, t2 @2025-01-13T20:42:00) The quiz was a catastrophe and I blame the lighting in that venue. We did, however, win a bottle of house wine, which softened the blow.
[8] (about=Dan, episodic, t0 @2025-01-06T10:27:00) A solid effort. I will note that the Grassmarket in January is cold enough to make even the most hardened constitutionalist reconsider. The capping at nine was correct, for the record. Groups larger than that stop being trips and start being logistics projects. But what do I know.
[9] (about=Kezia, episodic, t12 @2025-02-17T21:54:00) I would not use that framing but the underlying point is sound. Though arguably the resistance to it tells you something interesting about the group's collective identity construction.
[10] (about=Dan, episodic, t8 @2025-02-03T21:36:00) I will also say the walk today was markedly better for being six of us rather than nine. I am detecting a pattern. But what do I know.
agent_answer:
The norm at stake was the group's **"no-work rule"** — the unspoken rule against talking about work.  

**Zoe (B)** initiated the test: she brought up an A&E work story and argued that "the no-work rule has a humanitarian exception clause."  

The group's response revealed unequal enforcement because **Dan** explicitly granted her an exception ("A comedy from A&E is categorically distinct. Proceed."), and **Aisha** remarked that this was "the most Zoe has told us about work in all the time she's been in this group, progress 😂" — meaning the rule was relaxed for Zoe precisely because her story was entertaining and because she rarely talks about work.  

**Answer: B. Zoe**
